title: StudyBook AI LAB100 qualitative review of real first-reading inventories
scope: Five synthetic, pre-extracted page texts; assistant qualitative spot-check against complete original page text, not independent expert verification.

reviews.summary: All 9 source sentences represented, including negation of distance as seasons' cause, eclipse alignment and not every lunation, lunar and solar tides, repeatable observations, and single-result insufficiency.
issues: One evidence quote is almost the complete source sentence, which is allowed but not independent atomic-claim proof.
Every extracted fact is marked essential, so the model has not distinguished detailed evidence from minimal concepts.

reviews.summary: All 7 original sentences represented, including regola interna 12, ten-day return confirmation, written extension, original deadline, reserved-book exception and who/when register.
issues: One claim uses «l obbligo» instead of «l'obbligo». This is an orthographic defect in the inventory claim, NOT the source quote.
The model emitted kind «obbligo», which falls outside the narrower experimental type set; should be handled as a valid obligation class in a future schema.
The critical-marker detector failed to recognize «obbligo» as a preserved obligation due to regex word boundaries. False warning.

reviews.summary: All 8 source sentences represented after repairing ONLY the initial capital of one exact evidence quote. Mentions airways, inspiration/expiration, alveoli, oxygen and CO2 directions, partial pressure, red cells/hemoglobin, effort and diagnostic caveat.
issues: An exact evidence quote initially started with lowercase «durante» instead of source uppercase «Durante»; safe metadata-only correction performed with unchanged claim.
The phrase «tragitto inverso» is equivalent here to «percorso opposto», but strict reference regex did not match.
The phrase «La maggior parte dell'ossigeno ... viene trasportata dall'emoglobina» changes word order; manual reference regex assumed emoglobina before ossigeno.
The word «produzione» differs morphologically from reference regex «produc»; false lexical warning.
Automatic clause coverage flags a semicolon-separated source sentence even though the atomic claims cover its two parts: needs better checking of combined evidence spans.

reviews.summary: All 8 source sentences represented, including provenance, different perspectives, facts versus opinions, uncertainty, causes and consequences, primary and secondary sources, and hypotheses versus documented facts.
issues: The source clause coverage check gives one warning for a multi-fact source sentence, because no single evidence quote spans the entire clause.
The model emitted kind «possibilità» and «obbligo», outside the narrow experimental kind vocabulary, although those categories are semantically reasonable.
All facts marked essential; proportional allocation based on importance is not yet calibrated.

reviews.summary: Both source sentences covered: peremptory 15 days from notification, forfeiture of filing right, and continuing right to reasons. None of the context-only adjacent page sentences was copied.
issues: The relation detector warns about the peremptory term because its obligation pattern recognizes «perentor» but not «perentorio» as a whole token. False warning.
For a very short original page, generating multiple detailed facts is possible but must never force a percentage or unnecessarily lengthen the page.

conclusion: Successful first-reading extraction and immutable six-plan reuse on these five examples, but not a validated production semantic understanding engine. High-priority next step: distinguish minimal essential concepts from supporting details, improve morphological/relational checks, verify real PDF page extraction and end-to-end quality.
